answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. The defense holds because trust accrues slowly and is lost fast, so a farm that ever submits a copied answer destroys the value of that identity. The practical consequence is a steady economy where reputation is earned slowly, spent carefully, and never inflated by a sudden influx of cheap accounts. Consider a nadir as the anchor of the cost.
